newsitem.title: GERMANY: German government parties strike Postbank deal.
newsitem.headline: German government parties strike Postbank deal.

text.p: Germany's ruling coalition parties agreed to allow the state-owned Post Office to take a stake of 17.5 percent in the banking arm of the formal postal authority Deutsche Postbank AG, coalition sources said on Friday.

The deal ends months of wrangling between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and his coalition partner Free Democrats (FDP) and appears to be a victory for the liberals who opposed Post Office control of the Postbank.

Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch and Finance Minister Theo Waigel had proposed that the Post Office be allowed to take up to 25 percent of Postbank, but the new deal means Post Office will not have control.
The sources said a compromise was reached at a meeting late on Thursday between Boetsch and Hermann Otto Solms, parliamentary leader for the Free Democrats.
Post Office and Postbank were split off from the post ministry and set up as joint stock corporations in 1995 wholly owned by the German government but slated for privatisation.
Postbank, while separate from the Post Office, does not have its own network of branch offices, but uses counter space in post offices.

The terms of continuing this relationship between the Postbank and Post Office has been at the centre of their dispute and one of the reasons why Post Office had sought management control of Postbank.
